title: Adoption Success Framework — 90-day Customer Sprint Plan
content:
Executive summary:

This document is a pragmatic, outcome-centered 90-day onboarding sprint framework designed for mid-market and enterprise customers using Redwood Inference. It focuses on measurable activation milestones, clear owner responsibilities, rapid risk detection, and lightweight rituals that scale across multiple concurrent onboards. The goal: move customers from initial signup to a production inference path with measurable cost and latency baselines and a plan for renewal conversations starting month two.

Key principles (how this differs from a standard checklist):
- Outcome-first: every activity maps to a customer-visible outcome (e.g., "first successful private deployment" or "<50ms p95 for smoke load").
- Small experiments: 1 hypothesis per sprint for performance/cost optimizations to avoid scope creep.
- Early renewal signals: bake renewal indicators into week-4 and week-8 checkpoints.
- Shared accountability: CS + Solutions + Eng owners with explicit SLAs for responses.

Success objectives (90-day):
- O1: Customer completes a validated proof-of-concept run using the target model family and workload shape (acceptance: reproducible runbook + sample inputs/outputs).
- O2: Achieve baseline SLO targets for production demo workload (example: p95 latency <= target, token cost within budget delta).
- O3: Integrate Redwood SDK or API into one product path and confirm 1 internal stakeholder uses it weekly (engagement).
- O4: Identify at least one cost-optimization with >=10% unit-cost improvement without >5% degradation in output quality.

Primary metrics to track (KPI strings):
- Time-to-first-successful-inference (days)
- Activation-rate (percentage of target users completing integration tasks)
- p95-latency-ms (baseline & latest)
- tokens-per-inference (avg)
- Monthly API calls expected vs. observed (consumption curve)
- Chance-of-renewal score (0-100) - qualitative + signals mapped

Owners and roles (single-line owners):
- CS Lead: Maya Chen — overall adoption & renewal cadence owner
- Solutions Engineer (SE): Priya Nair — integration and demo success
- Technical PM / Customer Eng: Jared Park — runbook, deployment troubleshooting, internal escalations
- Account Exec: Sophie Müller — commercial touchpoints, renewal prep
- SRE/Infra buddy: assigned per customer from platform-eng when private/dedicated mode is used

90-day sprint breakdown (outcomes + acceptance criteria):
- Sprint 0 (Pre-kickoff, days -7 to 0):
  - Outcome: Kickoff materials and sandbox credentials provisioned, initial success criteria agreed.
  - Acceptance: Access verified, kickoff agenda set, key stakeholders confirmed.
  - Tasks: provisioning, data classification survey, security checklist sent, Jira project created.

- Sprint 1 (Day 1-30): Core integration + first-run
  - Outcome: Customer hits first successful end-to-end inference with sample traffic.
  - Acceptance: Reproducible runbook + logs showing a successful run, basic metrics recorded.
  - Tasks: kickoff meeting, SDK walkthrough, sample prompt library creation, run simple smoke tests, record latency & token counts, one short enablement session for product team.
  - Risk signals: no SDK integration after 7 days, missing credentials, test errors > 3 distinct failures.

- Sprint 2 (Day 31-60): Harden for repeatability and scale
  - Outcome: Deterministic behavior under target throughput and basic observability configured.
  - Acceptance: Load test at 50% of expected production throughput with p95 latency within SLO, console dashboards configured, alert thresholds set.
  - Tasks: ramp tests, KV/cache suggestions applied, batching config trial, training on console dashboards, set up tracing hooks.
  - Optimization experiment: try 1 quantization/variant and measure cost/quality delta with A/B.
  - Renewal signal checkpoint: customer confirms value milestones; Account Exec schedules renewal-intent meeting in week 9 if positive.

- Sprint 3 (Day 61-90): Productionization + handoff to success/ops
  - Outcome: Repeatable deployment path validated and runbook handed to internal ops; cost baseline documented; roadmap for next 90 days agreed.
  - Acceptance: Runbook + rollback steps, SLA/latency baseline doc, cost projection, and one post-mortem on the integration.
  - Tasks: finalize rollout policy (canary/baseline), document fallback models, schedule quarterly review, capture lessons learned.

Onboarding checkpoints and rituals (short bullets):
- Day 0 kickoff (30–45m): agenda + roles + success criteria + short demo.
- Weekly 30m sync (weeks 1–8): quick blockers, metrics, next-steps; use a shared Jira board.
- Bi-weekly deep dive (30–60m) during ramp weeks: SE-led, record action items.
- 60-day technical health check: sign-off by SRE/Infra buddy.
- 75-day commercial check: Account Exec aligns on renewal approach.

Lightweight templates (copyable snippets):
- Kickoff agenda: intros (5m), goals & success criteria (10m), demo overview (10m), immediate blockers + next steps (10m).
- Sample acceptance criteria checklist: credentials verified, SDK integrated, first inference logged, baseline metrics recorded, runbook URL present.

Risk ladder and mitigation actions (concise):
- Low risk (on track): continue planned experiments.
- Medium risk (missed sprint deadline): escalate to SE + CS Lead, schedule immediate war-room call, propose remediation task list.
- High risk (no integration at day 30 or negative cost/quality): involve Platform Eng, propose temporary hosted fallback, map to contract owner for churn mitigation.

Renewal indicators and tracker fields (to be surfaced in CRM):
- Adoption milestones complete (Y/N)
- Usage trend (up/down/flat)
- Performance vs SLO (ok/warning/breach)
- Commercial engagement (last contact date)
- Support volume (none/low/medium/high)
- Strategic alignment (stop/maintain/expand)

Quick-play escalation mapping (one-liners):
- Support tickets > 3 in 5 days -> SE triage within 8 business hours.
- p95 latency breach -> notify SRE, open incident channel, temporary rollback to fallback model.
- Cost spike > 50% week-over-week -> pause non-critical batch jobs, investigate cache/batching.

Sample outreach snippets (short, copy/paste friendly):
- Day 1 kickoff invite: "Hi <Customer>, excited to get started — join us on <date> to align on goals and confirm access. Agenda attached."
- Week-2 nudge: "Quick check — did you hit the first inference? If not, I can hop on a 20m screen-share to unblock."

Operational artifacts to create per customer (minimum):
- Single-run runbook (markdown link)
- Jira board with labelled tasks: onboarding, integration-bugs, perf-experiment, docs
- Shared dashboard in Redwood Console (read-only to customer ops)
- Cost projection spreadsheet (3-month view)

Acceptance criteria for 'ready for renewal discussion' (short list):
- 60%+ of acceptance checklist items complete.
- Usage indicates sustained activity across 2+ product owners.
- Technical lead confirms production path and rollback plan.

Experiment log template (one-line rows):
- Experiment name | hypothesis | metric | baseline | result | next-step

Appendix A — Common checklist (single-line items):
- NDA signed (if private deployment)
- IP/network allowlist configured
- KMS/HSM key handshake done
- Console access set for named users
- Cost alerts configured
- Training session recorded and uploaded

Appendix B — Example metrics baseline (example numbers, for reference only):
- First successful inference: day 6
- p95 latency: 210ms (smoke) -> target 120ms
- tokens-per-inference: 320 avg
- monthly projected calls: 120k

Notes to CS reps (short, pragmatic):
- Don’t promise specific model latencies until runbook load tests complete.
- Always surface cost tradeoffs when proposing quantization or batching changes.
- Keep renewal dialog technical in week 8 (metrics) and commercial in week 10 (terms).

Open questions / backlog items (items to capture during reviews):
- Should we automate the renewal-intent scheduling when the 60% checklist threshold is hit?
- Template for quantization A/B testing in dashboards (ownership: Product-Optimize).
- Lightweight privacy questionnaire to standardize pre-provision checks for private deployments.

Last checked-in: 2026-02-18 by Maya Chen.
